Boundary: cartesian_vector_components_3d (signed parent) supplies components, cited not re-derived. RECIPROCAL BOUNDARY with cross_product_moment_3d (signed earlier this batch) is stated in the artifact: that skill uses a dot product ONLY as a perpendicularity check and computes no projection, while this skill owns the dot product as a projection tool and computes no moment or cross product - naming the complement was required because the sibling already states its half. unit_vector_along_line (downstream, planned) owns FORMING a unit direction; this skill uses the general form (A . B)/|B|, which needs no unit vector, and never binds or constructs one. The VECTOR projection (scalar times a unit direction) therefore requires that ceded construction and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE - the deliverable is the signed SCALAR projection. position_vector_3d, coordinate_direction_angles and cartesian_vector_addition_3d excluded. Worked example Operator-re-derived from the on-disk prompt: A = -6i -6j -3k (|A| = 9), B = 2i +2j -1k (|B| = 3); A . B = (-6)(2) + (-6)(2) + (-3)(-1) = -12 - 12 + 3 = -21; A_par = -21/3 = -7; cos theta = -21/27 = -7/9 = -0.7778 -> theta = 141.1 deg. HONEST LIMITATION recorded: the bound catches an undivided product sum (21 > 9) and a sign-dropped product sum (27/3 = 9, not strictly less than 9) but does NOT catch dividing by |A| instead of |B| (2.33 < 9 passes while being wrong) - stated as a property of the check rather than overstated. Procedure step 4 (the in-plane split) is deliberately LEFT UNMAPPED: that is vector_components_2d's content, and a student failing there needs the parent skill, which already diagnoses it — the same principle applied on support_reactions_2d. SIGNAL-POLICY DEBT recorded per Architect Batch 4E Decision B: a theta-swap at step 4 yields (48, -36, 80), which is wrong AND closes the magnitude check, so no signal on this skill catches it. Mapping a duplicate axis_confusion there is forbidden by Decision B, and inventing a signal is not authorized; the hole is recorded rather than forced. Review-beat correction: the draft used alpha for the angle from +z while common_errors warned students against the coordinate direction angles alpha/beta/gamma — but those are conventionally measured from +x/+y/+z, so the angle this skill called alpha is conventionally gamma. The artifact was using a coordinate-direction-angle symbol for a different meaning while telling students that convention belongs elsewhere, and coordinate_direction_angles is a downstream node this skill unlocks, where alpha will mean angle-from-+x. Renamed to phi, the standard polar angle from +z, which pairs conventionally with theta azimuthal. Alpha now survives only inside the literal string alpha/beta/gamma where it correctly names the other skill's convention.
